items.title: 蔡康永稱「沒支持過台獨」後出席蔣萬安造勢 兩岸輿論未息
items.description: 分析人士稱，「這根本不是一封求饒的『道歉信』，而是一封向特定市場與群眾溫柔清算的『道別信』」。
items.content:
蔡康永稱「沒有支持過台獨」後出席蔣萬安造勢活動 兩岸輿論仍未息
台灣主持人蔡康永因月初出席民進黨台北市長候選人沈伯洋競選總部成立大會，在華人輿論圈引發廣泛關注，並遭到中國官方點名及部分合作品牌切割。
10月25日深夜，他在微博與小紅書發表長文，強調自己「一直希望兩岸友好來往，我沒有支持過台獨」。
這篇聲明被視為兼具澄清與告別意味，但未能平息對岸輿論的不滿。前《環球時報》總編輯胡錫進持續發文批評，台灣輿論則有人將此事與2016年周子瑜事件類比。
26日下午，身穿黑色西裝、白色上衣的蔡康永如期出席蔣萬安的競總成立活動。
蔡康永說了什麼？
蔡康永的聲明以「致關心此事的你」為題，條列三點。他在開頭直接重申：「我一直希望兩岸友好來往。我沒有支持過台獨。」
現年64歲的蔡康永回顧，自1998年主持訪談節目至今，累積訪問近萬名立場各異的來賓，但「我從來沒有成為其中任何一位的信徒」。他強調，「拜訪對方並不表示會認同對方」，並就「誤會」對合作方及曾經喜歡他的人造成的困擾致歉。
聲明末段，他提到來自上海的父母原本互不相識，直到搬遷台北才相遇。「如果不是時代動盪形成的緣分，世上根本不會有我這個人。」他寫道，所有曾讓他被看見、被聽見的緣分，即使已告一段落，他永遠感激，並祝願一切安好。
藍綠陣營如何回應
針對蔡康永貼文，蔣萬安則於今日上午出席活動時受訪表示，歡迎蔡康永參加他的競總成立活動。「其實不論蔡康永先生支持或不支持我，我都尊重他的言論還有政治立場」。
蔣萬安進一步強調，他反對任何人因言論或政治立場不同，就動輒出征、抵制或杯葛他人。「我絕對不允許、絕不接受這樣反民主的威脅。」他並呼籲對岸尊重台灣自由民主的生活方式，不要因政治傾向而有差別待遇。
沈伯洋同日上午接受台媒聯訪時稱，蔡康永當天已把話說得十分明白，走訪現場純粹是為訪問不同陣營的政治人物、深入探討政見。
「這在民主社會的台灣本是再普通不過的日常，然而台灣人行使最平凡的自主權利，卻換來中國以這種手段施壓干預，令人深感痛心。」沈伯洋說。
來自學界、長期研究中國認知作戰、近年遭中國公開「通緝」的沈伯洋特別指出，蔡康永的發文時間點「絕非自主決定，而是被決定的」。他認為，該貼文發出後隨即登上微博熱搜榜首，而微博熱搜前三名本質上由中國官方掌控，「無論被迫或另有隱情，中國企圖干涉台灣民眾自主抉擇的痕跡極為明顯」。
蔡康永在微博有約3500萬粉絲。
大陸網友：不領情
然而，這篇聲明並未獲得對岸輿論領情。在小紅書上，大批網民湧入蔡康永的留言區，質疑他玩弄「雙面手法」，要求他將聲明同步發到Threads等台灣常用社交平台。
「把這篇『不支持台獨』搬到台灣大眾最常用的平台再說」、「依舊不敢說一句『我是中國人』」、「大玩說話的藝術：我爸媽是上海人，但我不是」，部分留言寫道。也有人直接建議：「發一個中國國旗得了，根本不用舉例子。」
中國國台辦之前已表態，任何人都不能一邊賺取大陸發展紅利，一邊與「台獨」分裂勢力勾連糾纏，做「兩面人」。
《環球時報》前總編輯胡錫進26日凌晨發文指出，蔡康永並未就其行為道歉，只是對合作方及粉絲因「誤會」產生的困擾表達歉意。他形容蔡康永「態度不軟、身段挺軟」，並未擺出對抗姿態，字裡行間透露出他自感難以重回大陸主持或參加綜藝節目，「這篇帖子有向粉絲告別的意味」。
胡錫進直言，這篇帖子若用來與合作方和粉絲「好合好散」則已足夠，若想扭轉輿論態度「那麼差遠了」。他還附上「蔡康永依舊沒有說一句我是中國人」的標籤。這篇貼文隨後被刪除。此前，胡錫進已多次批評蔡康永為「台獨頑固分子」沈伯洋站台，是「主動招惹是非、犯了大忌」。
台灣輿論：周子瑜事件翻版？
在台灣，有網友將此事與2016年周子瑜事件類比，認為蔡康永是在商業壓力下被迫低頭。風波發酵之初，已有人預言：「要把康永當成周子瑜了嗎？」
曾在杭州阿里巴巴工作多年的台灣財經網紅胡采蘋在臉書評論，這是「威逼廠商以迫使當事人『下跪』的手法」。
不過，中央大學中文系助理教授胡川安有不同解讀。他認為，這篇文字沒有「一絲討好或討饒的委屈，反倒充滿蔡康永一貫的冷靜與體面」。在他看來，蔡康永很清楚風波的終局，「這根本不是一封求饒的『道歉信』，而是一封向特定市場與群眾溫柔清算的『道別信』」。
台灣也不乏批評蔡康永的聲音。擁有百萬訂閱的網紅「Cheap」（鄭才暐）在臉書個人專頁表示，蔡康永這次「三頭不討好」，一口氣得罪了「小粉紅、綠粉、藍粉」。
他認為此事與周子瑜事件不同：「演藝圈靠話術和高情商確實能夠吃得開，但在政治圈可沒這麼容易。康永哥是主動搞這齣，真的很難把他當成『無辜受害者』來同情。」
另一位知名網紅陳沂則批評蔡康永「晚節不保」，稱「中國網友只會覺得你想要風骨又沒骨氣，文人之恥莫過於此」。這則貼文累積近萬人點讚。
夾縫中的台灣藝人
蔡康永風波並非孤立個案，而是台灣藝人在兩岸穿梭之間，言行被放大檢視、自願表態或「被表態」的縮影。
新加坡《聯合早報》刊出評論稱，就在沈伯洋競總成立前一天，台北警方搜查一家同志夜店，因執法爭議，蔣萬安事後出面道歉。台灣政論圈有人猜測，早已公開同志身分的蔡康永因為同志人權，才「憤而」現身沈伯洋造勢現場，暗示此事與統獨無關。
但評論也指出，即使蔡康永接著出席蔣萬安的活動，恐怕也難以安撫對岸輿情，因為兩岸輿論已陷入「非此即彼」的僵局。
與此同時，台灣陸委會正在收緊對相關言論的容忍範圍。2026年中國「十一」國慶前後，陸委會副主委梁文傑表示，掌握約19名藝人發文祝賀中國國慶，多為轉發央視模板，並重申兩條紅線：不能宣揚對台動武、不能宣揚消滅中華民國主權，踩線即查處。
台灣藝人吳奇隆近日高調在微博手持五星紅旗慶祝中國國慶，其後原定出席的台灣棒球賽開球活動因球迷抗議取消，主辦單位稱吳奇隆因身體因素無法出席。
根據台灣《兩岸人民關係條例》第33條之1，未經許可不得與中共黨政軍合作。
隨著年底地方選舉逼近，兩岸政治敏感度升高，台灣藝人與公眾人物無論主動表態或被動切割，這類風波的循環與升級可能成為常態，持續考驗當事人、代言品牌與台灣社會對相關言論的承受力。

items.title: 福田康夫逝世享年90歲 長期親華的「短暫」日本首相
items.description: 福田康夫出任日本首相期間才不過一年，當時曾被國內輿論批評為「不負責任」；北京讚揚其對中日關係「作出積極貢獻」。
items.content:
福田康夫逝世享年90歲 長期親華的「短暫」日本首相
日本執政自民黨宣佈，在2007至2008年間擔任日本首相的福田康夫已於近日逝世，享年90歲。
自民黨星期一（10月26日）公佈，福田康夫上星期四（22日）逝世，葬禮將僅安排近親參加。共同社等媒體引述消息人士稱，福田康夫因心臟功能衰竭，在東京一家醫院去世。
福田康夫從上任到辭任首相僅365天，且當時曾招致批評，但中日媒體均指出其致力改善兩國關係，包括促成時任中國國家主席胡錦濤訪問日本。
現任日本首相高市早苗讚揚福田康夫在任期間「竭盡所能」；中國外交部稱呼其為「中國人民的老朋友」。
改善中日關係的「終身事業」
福田康夫2007年9月26日就任日本首相，2008年9月24日卸任，前後僅365天。但在此之前，他擔任內閣官房長官三年半，是自由民主黨政權迄今任期第二長的官房長官。
福田康夫是在安倍晉三辭去其首次任期後當上執政自民黨黨總裁與日本首相。他被視為外交「鴿派」，在任內主張改善週邊尤其是對華關係。
福田康夫迴避安倍晉三修改和平憲法以促進海外軍事部署等較具野心的政策，又促成了胡錦濤到訪，那是時隔十年來首次有中國國家元首訪日。
2007年8月15日——二戰日本戰敗投降紀念日——兩位自民黨籍前首相前首相小泉純一郎和安倍晉三先後參拜了供奉有二戰甲級戰犯的東京靖國神社，福田康夫則拒絕前往參拜。
福田康夫在日本內閣任內也曾處理中日外交衝突：2001年4月，森喜朗內閣與小泉純一郎內閣交接之際，東京批准台灣前總統李登輝到訪，引起北京強烈不滿。作為政府首席發言人的內閣官房長官福田康夫為內閣辯護，稱是基於人道理由而向李登輝發出簽證。
1995年1月，仍只是眾議員的福田康夫曾訪問台灣，會晤李登輝。當時由中國國民黨執政的台灣總統府仍將訪問稱為「訪華」，官方新聞稿除了稱福田康夫「曾多次訪華」外，還稱他「擔任眾議員以來，經常給予我國支持與協助」。
2020年，李登輝逝世，福田康夫到台灣駐日本代表處弔唁。
共同社指出，由於在官房長官任內積極推動官邸外交，福田康夫這位發言人也被稱為「影子外相」。
End of 2007年12月：福田康夫訪華
辭任首相後，福田康夫於2010年給中國參與創辦的博鰲亞洲論壇擔任理事長，並連任至2018年，卸任後留任論壇諮詢委員會主席。2025年3月，福田康夫仍有為博鰲論壇年會一場週邊會議發表書面致辭。
2014年7月，中國與日本再次因東海釣魚島（日本稱尖閣諸島；台灣稱釣魚台列嶼）主權爭議陷入外交僵局之際，福田康夫以博鰲論壇理事長身份訪華，秘密替二度出任日本首相的安倍晉三傳話，呼籲現任中國國家主席習近平同意對話。
2025年11月，高市早苗首相發表「台灣有事」論，引起中國強烈不滿，中日關係一直陷於低谷。在《每日新聞》今年1月刊出對福田康夫的專訪中，福田康夫說：「高市早苗首相究竟有沒有預料到中國會作出如此強烈的反應？我感覺她或許是在沒有考慮到那種程度的情況下發表相關言論的。」
「或許連中方也沒想到事態會陷入如此僵局。這真是一件令人遺憾的事。」
報導稱，福田康夫在專訪中也反問了究竟是哪一方製造了對立的火種。
日本放送協會（NHK）形容，加強日中關係是其「畢生志業」。
在星期一的例行記者會上，中國外交部對福田康夫逝世表示「沉痛哀悼」。
外交部發言人郭嘉昆說：「福田康夫先生是中國人民的老朋友，為推動中日關係改善發展作出積極貢獻。他長期心系中日友好、秉持正確歷史觀，擔任首相期間簽署了中日第四份政治文件，卸任後參觀了侵華日軍南京大屠殺遇難同胞紀念館。」
郭嘉昆不點名批評高市早苗說：「福田康夫先生曾指出，中日四個政治文件規定了兩國關係遵循的原則，必須時刻牢記，不能走回頭路。這一表態擲地有聲，體現了日本老一輩政治家的信義和擔當，日本當政者應當深思自省。」
台灣總統賴清德透過社交平台X對福田康夫逝世表達「深切哀悼」。
「台日之間由深厚情誼緊密相連。期盼今後雙方交流與合作進一步深化，並願這份無可替代的友誼長久延續。」
「前無古人」的首相父子
據NHK報導，高市早苗對福田康夫辭世感到「悲痛」。
高市早苗在首相官邸對記者說：「在豐富的經驗和卓越的見識基礎上，即使面對極其困難的課題，他也始終竭盡所能，一項一項持續推動相關工作。」
「作為北海道洞爺湖峰會主席，他也大力向世界展現了我國的存在感。」
高市早苗所指的，是2008年7月舉行的八大工業國組織（G8）領導人峰會——當時俄羅斯仍未被排除於集團之外。
福田康夫1936年7月16日生於東京，祖籍群馬縣高崎市，父親福田赳夫最初是代表群馬縣選區的眾議院議員，後來出任首相。
儘管出身政治世家，福田年輕時對職業政治並沒有太大興趣，在石油公司以「上班族」身分度過了17年。
然而，原本被培養成政治接班人，過繼他人的弟弟橫手征夫染上重病後，福田康夫接手成為父親的秘書，並跟隨其進入首相官邸任職。
1990年，福田赳夫退休，當時53歲的福田康夫接替父親參選，並首次當選眾議員。
福田康夫先後給森喜朗和小泉純一郎兩任首相擔任官房長官，其中小泉純一郎任內發生美國911恐怖襲擊，福田康夫被日本媒體視為該國應對後續影響的主要人物。
當小泉純一郎的繼任人安倍晉三宣佈辭職，福田康夫宣佈競逐黨總裁，旋即獲得黨內不同派系支持。他的當選，使福田家成為日本憲政史上首個父子先後出任首相的家族。
但在他出選時，被外界形容為以脾氣急躁見稱的福田康夫曾笑說，面對國會朝野分立、在野黨有能力拖延立法進程的景況，他當選首相「也許是抽到了下下籤呢」。
2008年，沖繩發生駐日美軍士兵涉嫌強姦14歲女孩事件，福田康夫對此表示「不可饒恕」，但他曾在2003年被國內媒體曝光其私下稱，一些女性衣著暴露自招強姦，「穿成那種樣子的人自己也有問題」。
作為一個鴿派人物，福田康夫除了主張與中國修補關係外，也對朝鮮（北韓）採取較靈活立場，尤其是在嘗試解決1970至1980年代平壤綁架問題方面。
在立法施政受制於在野黨派之下，福田康夫執政風格顯得被動，其任內爆發的一連串醜聞也逐步侵蝕其民望：年金紀錄遺失、軍方賄賂醜聞，以及一項因增加老年人負擔而引發強烈不滿的醫療制度改革。
2008年4月至6月間，日本經濟出現萎縮，只要多持續一個季度，日本便技術上進入經濟衰退。8月的內閣改組曾短暫提振福田政府的聲勢，但在此過程中，他也提拔了自己的競爭對手麻生太郎。
2008年9月1日深夜，福田康夫宣佈辭任首相，輿論譁然。一些評論指責他「放棄政權」，《每日新聞》更形容其行為屬「毫無信念的政治漂流」。9月24日，麻生太郎當選首相，正式接替福田康夫。
一年後，日本舉行大選，福田康夫並未參選，且正式宣佈退出政壇，由長子福田達夫繼承衣缽。

items.title: 中共五中全會開幕：十三年反腐後，如何繼續「從嚴治黨」？
items.description: 中國政壇至今沒有明確的接班人。受訪專家認為，這反映習近平面臨兩難：不指定接班人有助維持權威，指定接班人則可能提前形成新的權力中心。
items.content:
中共五中全會開幕：十三年反腐後，如何繼續「從嚴治黨」？
中共二十屆五中全會星期一（10月26日）在北京開幕，會期至29日。這次全會以「全面從嚴治黨」為主題。
按官方通報，全會將審議《關於持之以恆推進全面從嚴治黨的決定》文件。對於中共而言，以「決定」為名的文件，須由中央全會審議，通常用於某一領域的重大部署，一屆中央委員會五年內只有少數幾份。這份《決定》要到全會閉幕才會正式通過並公布。
開幕前數月，反腐行動明顯加密。8月27日，江西省長葉建春被查；10月13日，已退休的前重慶市長黃奇帆也被宣布接受調查。近年落馬的中管幹部人數持續攀升。外界關注，中共如何總結過去的反腐成果，以及這場會議為明年換屆釋放哪些信號？
美國喬治亞州立大學政治學教授安德魯·魏德曼（Andrew Wedeman）長期研究中國政治與反腐運動。他對BBC中文表示，近幾年被查的「老虎」數量屢創新高，反腐的力度和速度遠超以往任何時期。「這意味著兩件事：第一，反腐運動確實抓到了很多人；第二，它並沒有成功發揮威懾作用。」
分析人士認為，北京正透過會前的反腐行動，進一步整頓官僚體系，並處理二十一大前的人事問題。但十三年反腐之後，仍有三個關鍵問題沒有答案：習近平能否讓官僚體系真正按他的意志運作？十三年反腐後，腐敗是否減少、威懾是否有效？退休官員是否仍有安全空間？
「黨建」主題：從制定政策到落實政策
按照慣例，五中全會本應聚焦下一個五年規劃。但本屆三中全會延遲，四中、五中全會的議題依次順延。四中全會已審議通過「十五五」規劃建議，五中全會因此承接通常屬於六中全會的黨建議題。官方已明確，會議將審議《中共中央關於持之以恆推進全面從嚴治黨若干重大問題的決定》。
魏德曼認為，這反映習近平當前最關注的已不只是制定新政策，而是如何確保政策得以落實。習近平近年多次批評地方官員「陽奉陰違」、「自行其是」。在魏德曼看來，北京真正希望解決的不只是腐敗，更是官僚體系的執行力。
亞洲協會政策研究所中國政治研究員牛犇（Neil Thomas）在發給BBC中文的電郵中預測，全會後可能出現幾項變化：重大項目和財政支出的監管加強，黨委書記的問責機制強化，更多利用大數據查處腐敗，地方官員面對更嚴格的監管，紀檢部門的權力進一步擴大。
不過他也提醒，如此嚴厲的問責制度，可能令基層官員更不願承擔風險。
十三年反腐，如何繼續「從嚴治黨」
中共反腐在習近平2012年底上台之後，開啟「風暴」模式，「打虎拍蠅」成為中國人耳熟能詳的政治語碼。「老虎」通常指中央管理的副部級以上官員；「蒼蠅」指查處基層腐敗官員。
落馬的中管官員人數近年持續攀升，根據中紀委披露，2025年立案審查調查的中管幹部181人，比2024年的92人增加近一倍。同期立案縣處級幹部4.1萬人，立案鄉科級幹部13.7萬人。
魏德曼說：「過去十幾年裡，習近平的反腐運動累積了驚人的戰果，但他並沒有贏得這場戰爭。」他指出，反腐的目的不只是查處，更在形成威懾，讓涉腐者收手，讓未涉腐者不敢越界，但高官落馬數量長期居高不下，說明這一效果沒有達到預期。他說，許多今天落馬的「老虎」，在中層任上就已涉腐，有的持續十年、十五年，期間不僅逃過查處，還一路升遷。
對於外界所說的「越反越腐」，他並不認為是反腐催生了更多腐敗。更準確的說法是，十三年高壓反腐，仍未完全改變官員的行為模式。
被污染的池子中，如何選人？
魏德曼認為，習近平如今面對的，已不再主要是前任時期提拔的官員。「現在他真正不得不面對的，是那些在他任內被提拔上來的人當中的腐敗問題。」他形容，習近平把落馬的「老虎」清除，再提拔新人接替，卻發現自己是在一個已被污染的池子裡挑人。在他看來，問題未必只存在於個別官員或特定派系，而可能與整個幹部選拔機制有關。
他還留意到，許多落馬官員近年公開發表的懺悔錄，敘事高度相似：從懷抱理想、服務人民開始，進入體制後逐步受環境影響，最終走向腐敗，落馬後完成悔悟。他認為，這種公式化的自白，反映官方傾向把腐敗歸因於個人道德失守。但如果大量官員講述幾乎相同的故事，問題是否僅在個人道德？
他分析，改革開放後的經濟高速增長和市場化，改變了官員的激勵方式。相比毛澤東時代強調的集體主義和奉獻精神，如今許多官員更傾向於把個人、家庭和未來發展納入考量。習近平透過意識形態教育和黨建工作，試圖重建官員的服從意識與使命感，但魏德曼認為效果並不明顯。
牛犇同樣認為，反腐如今已是持續性的組織整頓機制，而不再是派系鬥爭。於是，五中全會再次強調「全面從嚴治黨」，一個難以迴避的問題是：中共能否改變滋生腐敗的制度環境和官僚文化，還是只能繼續靠更嚴格的監督與懲罰維持運轉？
「安全著陸」不再存在？
會前，葉建春、曾與薄熙來共事的黃奇帆相繼被查，外界討論「安全著陸」是否已不復存在。
香港大學政治與公共行政學系副教授朱江南表示，目前這一輪密集的反腐傳遞出即使退休、離任也沒有所謂安全著陸的訊號，表達中央反腐沒有放鬆的意圖。
魏德曼說，他從不相信中共官場存在真正的安全著陸，1995年的陳希同、2006年的陳良宇，以及後來的周永康、薄熙來都是例證。
至於黃奇帆為何落馬，他認為目前很難判斷：可能與重慶任期有關，可能與上海時期有關，可能與退休後的金融圈人脈有關，也可能純粹是「政治祭旗」。
牛犇則認為，黃奇帆是專業技術官僚，他的落馬顯示當下的反腐已超越傳統派系劃分，更聚焦政治忠誠、風險控制和組織紀律。
五中全會也是觀察二十一大前人事布局的重要窗口。近年多名中央委員落馬，部分政治局職位出現空缺，這些位置是否會有新安排，是外界關注的焦點。
此外，中國政壇至今沒有明確的接班人。魏德曼和牛犇都認為，這反映習近平面臨兩難：不指定接班人有助維持權威，指定接班人則可能提前形成新的權力中心。

items.title: 巴西總統盧拉：北京在美國後院的「老朋友」第四次贏得大選
items.description: 盧拉總統意外獲勝，但他將面對一個充滿敵意的國會和一個兩極分化的國家。
items.content:
巴西總統盧拉：北京在美國後院的「老朋友」第四次贏得大選
  - Author, 瑪麗娜·羅西（Marina Rossi）
  - Role, BBC巴西葡語記者
  - Reporting from, 聖保羅報導
  - Author, 利安德羅·普拉澤雷斯（Leandro Prazeres）
  - Role, BBC巴西葡語記者
  - Reporting from, 巴西利亞報導
  - Author, 瓦妮莎·布施呂特（Vanessa Buschschlüter）
  - Role, BBC拉丁美洲網上新聞編輯
  - Reporting from, 倫敦報導
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
在經過一場激烈角逐的競選之後，巴西資深左翼總統路易斯·伊納西奧·盧拉·達席爾瓦（Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva；勞拉）成功連任，擊敗了尚未承認敗選的右翼對手弗拉維奧·博索納羅（Flávio Bolsonaro；博爾索納羅）。
巴西高等選舉法院（Superior Electoral Court）宣布，在所有選票點算完畢後，盧拉獲得51.79%的選票，而博索納羅獲得48.21%。
但博索納羅拒絕承認選舉結果，稱投票延長兩小時「無法解釋」——儘管他的競選團隊以及其對手的競選團隊都曾要求投票站延長開放時間。他在巴西利亞向支持者表示，他將尋求撤銷此次選舉。
然而，這並未阻止盧拉及其支持者慶祝他們所稱的「歷史性勝利」和一次出人意料的逆轉勝。
在勝選演說中，將於星期二（10月27日）滿81歲的盧拉讚揚年輕選民走上街頭「捍衛巴西民主」。
他通往第四個任期的道路並不平坦。自巴西於1988年恢復民主以來，他是首位在第一輪投票落敗卻最終贏得總統大選的領導人。而他再次當選、展開額外第二個任期，也屬前所未有。
他還逆轉了拉丁美洲更廣泛的趨勢——在該地區，選民紛紛懲罰執政者並轉向右翼。整個地區內，阿根廷、智利和哥倫比亞等大國如今都由保守派領導人執掌。
「我們的喉嚨都很疲倦了。」在勝選演說中，盧拉以沙啞的嗓音開場。
他幾乎立刻把麥克風交給副總統傑拉爾多·阿爾克明（Geraldo Alckmin），說希望由阿爾克明先發言。
阿爾克明對盧拉說：「你第二次拯救了巴西民主。」盧拉隨後感謝競選團隊的統籌者，也感謝「巴西人民的慷慨」，其中包括「走上街頭捍衛巴西民主」的年輕人。
他對群眾說，人們之所以投票，是因為我們能夠說服他們，這一票對我們國家的主權很重要。
他說，這場選舉是「消極情緒與謊言的失敗」。盧拉在勝選演說中再次強調，巴西「不會接受成為任何人的後院」。
這是他在競選期間一再重複的說法之一，指向「美國的後院」一詞，用來概括美國政策中一種觀念：拉丁美洲應處於美國的勢力範圍之內。
盧拉的競選活動在首輪失利後重新煥發生機，其動力來自街頭示威和大規模的社交媒體攻勢。
這位前金屬工人自1989年首次參選總統以來一直是巴西左翼的主導人物，然而，他現在面對的是自2003年首次執政以來最具挑戰性的政治格局。
他將於2027年1月5日開始的新任期，將在國內外重重掣肘之下展開，其中包括來自美國總統唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）的敵意。
雖然特朗普並未直接為盧拉的對手弗拉維奧·博索納羅背書——他曾在哥倫比亞和洪都拉斯舉行的總統選舉中為最終獲勝的右翼候選人背書——但幾乎可以肯定，他的政府更希望看到一位保守派執掌這個擁有2.13億人口的國家。
白宮將拉丁美洲視為美國的勢力範圍，特朗普政府熱切希望支持其政策的領導人上台執政，包括在國防、安全和貿易方面的政策。
美國政府還熱切希望削弱中國在西半球的影響力。
巴西石油資源豐富，並擁有全球第二大稀土礦物儲量，是南美洲唯一非右翼領導人執政的大國，而盧拉在很大程度上被視為對華友好。
弗拉維奧·博索納羅曾承諾讓巴西與華盛頓結盟，而盧拉則警告美國不要干預選舉，並堅稱巴西「絕不會成為任何人的後院」。
不過，儘管白宮可能感到失望，盧拉的勝利將受到環保人士的歡迎。他們曾擔心，博索納羅若勝選，將使巴西頗具影響力的農業綜合企業和採礦業獲得更大權力。
他們曾指出，在博索納羅的父親雅伊爾（Jair Bolsonaro）擔任總統期間，亞馬遜地區的森林砍伐和森林火災創下紀錄水平，並認為在這位較年輕的博索納羅治下，更寬鬆的環境政策可能再次導致這一關鍵生態系統遭到破壞。
儘管盧拉的支持者對他的勝利欣喜若狂，但選舉結果顯示這個國家仍然深度分裂，超過48%的選民選擇了博索納羅。
除了團結這個如此嚴重極化國家的挑戰之外，盧拉還將不得不與巴西民主時代最右翼的國會同朝執政。
博索納羅的自由黨（PL）是此次選舉中斬獲最多的政黨。
然而，盧拉的勞工黨（Workers' Party）在決選前成功組織了大型集會，顯示出該黨所擁有的強大基層支持。
選舉前，盧拉曾將這次投票形容為「巴西的分水嶺」。
他承諾以「新的治理方式」彌合巴西對立政治陣營之間的鴻溝，並在選前的一場WhatsApp直播中補充說，「這個國家將不會再是原來的樣子」。
雖然他幾乎沒有提供有關新治理方式具體內容的細節，但他堅稱自己將「堅定不移地為建設一個更公正的國家而奮鬥，讓人人都有機會，讓政策以民眾的需求為導向」。
面對一個大致上充滿敵意的國會，這場奮鬥對這位資深領導人來說——其第四任期結束時將年滿85歲——可能會比他此前三次執政時期艱難得多。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。
盧拉：北京在美國後院的「老朋友」
BBC 中文記者陳岩
盧拉這個名字，在中國並不陌生。作為巴西左翼的代表，盧拉一向樂於與中國發展良好關係。
2023年4月，他對北京進行國事訪問，這是他時隔12年重新執政後，首次出訪美洲以外的國家，習近平在那次會談中稱他為「老朋友」。
盧拉與中國之間還有一重連接：羅塞夫（Dilma Rousseff）。
2023年那次訪問期間，盧拉專程前往上海，出席羅塞夫出任新開發銀行行長的就職典禮。羅塞夫被視為盧拉一手提攜的政治接班人，2011年至2016年任巴西總統，卸任後加入新開發銀行。
這家銀行由金磚國家（BRICs）於2015年成立，總部設在上海。不僅如此，2024年9月，習近平在北京人民大會堂向羅塞夫頒授「友誼勛章」。這是中國對外國人的最高國家榮譽，她也是該批授勛者中唯一的外國人。
頒獎儀式後不到兩個月，習近平便訪問巴西，受到盧拉的盛情接待。歡迎儀式上，巴西藝術家用中文演唱了《我的祖國》。2025年5月，盧拉再度國事訪華，這是他第六次到訪中國，也是同一任期內第二次訪華。
巴西與中國在農業（尤其是大豆）、礦產等出口產業上的貿易往來十分緊密，但其實盧拉始終強調戰略自主，避免選邊站隊。
盧拉任內，巴西並未直接加入「一帶一路」倡議。2024年11月習近平訪巴期間，雙方簽署合作規劃，把「一帶一路」與巴西的「加速增長計劃」等本國發展戰略對接。這顯示出盧拉的務實取向：既希望通過與中國合作獲取經濟利益，又堅持把主導權握在自己手裡。
中國資本也在加速進入巴西。據巴中企業家委員會統計，2024年中國對巴西直接投資同比增長113%，約42億美元，巴西躍升為中國全球第三大投資目的地；2025年增至61億美元，升至第一位。投資領域從石油、電力等傳統行業，擴展到新能源汽車、科技和可再生能源製造。比亞迪在巴伊亞州卡馬薩里（Camaçari, Bahia）的工廠，2025年10月下線了該公司全球第1400萬輛新能源汽車，這輛車最終交付給了盧拉本人。
另一方面，盧拉經常批評美國，也多次抨擊美元霸權，希望以金磚國家機制為支點，不必依附華盛頓。但他並未放棄與美國企業合作。
今年8月，盧拉推動的「巴西AI計劃」公布超級計算項目，總投資約23億雷亞爾（4.6億美元；30.9億元人民幣；151億元新台幣）。其中，里約熱內盧的先進計算中心交由華為和科大訊飛兩家中國企業合作建設。
另有約10億雷亞爾用於採購一台高性能超級計算機，外界預計將由美國企業英偉達中標。
同一項戰略安排同時納入中美企業，說明即便與北京關係密切，盧拉也沒有在中美之間一邊倒。
這一邏輯同樣適用於此次大選中盧拉的對手弗拉維奧·博索納羅。這位參議員是前總統博索納羅的長子，與父親一脈相承，強調國家安全和深化對美合作，家族與特朗普交情甚篤，今年5月他剛在華盛頓與特朗普會面。
但選戰臨近，弗拉維奧也拒絕把外交描繪成中美二選一。他在9月明確表示，若當選，對華關係將以經濟務實為原則，「我們不必選邊」。
這也折射出許多中等國家面對中美競爭的心態：不願倒向任何一方成為附庸，而是希望成為兩邊都想爭取的對象，從中獲取更大收益。

items.title: 中國市場放緩，英國傳統精英私立學校紛紛進軍印度
items.description: 多所英國傳統精英私校近年相繼在印度開設分校，瞄準當地日益壯大的富裕階層。隨着中國教育監管收緊，加上英國私校面臨稅務壓力，印度成為新的擴張目標。
items.content:
中國市場放緩，英國傳統精英私立學校紛紛進軍印度
  - Author, 尼基爾·伊南達爾（Nikhil Inamdar）
  - Role, 印度孟買報道
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
位於印度西北部旁遮普邦（Punjab）昌迪加爾（Chandigarh）市郊，一間擁有473年歷史的英國傳統公學今年開設首個全女子國際校園。
與英格蘭貝德福德郡（Bedfordshire）校園內標誌性的哥德式中央建築相比，印度校舍採用較現代化設計，設有專門興建的教學大樓。但校園內一座醒目的紅磚鐘樓，仍保留著這所英國學校的傳統印記。
位於莫哈利（Mohali）的貝德福德學校（Bedford School）是最新一所在印度設校的英國公學。至少已有六所英國公學（歷史悠久的精英私立收費學校），包括三所在英國歷史最悠久的學校，近年陸續在印度各地開設校園。
它們的擴張，正值中國市場環境趨緊，以及英國自2025年1月1日起對私立學校學費徵收增值稅（VAT）之際。
自2023年起，素有印度「矽谷」之稱、匯聚大量軟件和初創企業的班加羅爾（Bengaluru），已成為著名的哈羅公學（Harrow School）在印度的據點。印度首任總理尼赫魯（Jawaharlal Nehru）便畢業於該校。
思貝禮學校（Shrewsbury School）則在印度中部城市博帕爾（Bhopal）設立校園；而威靈頓學院（Wellington College）選擇落戶浦那（Pune）。這座印度西部城市因擁有享負盛名的大學和學院而自稱為「東方牛津」。
據報，米爾菲爾德學校（Millfield）、伊利沙伯女王學校（Queen Elizabeth's School）以及其他幾所英國學校，未來數年亦將在印度開設分校。
數十年來，印度一直設有仿照英國殖民時期公學制度運作的寄宿學校，主要服務精英和貴族家庭。然而，隨著新興富裕階層壯大，愈來愈多印度家庭希望讓子女接觸更國際化的教育，市場亦迅速擴展。
哈羅公學的班加羅爾分校校長卡洛琳·帕斯科（Caroline Pascoe）向BBC表示：「我們的國際課程對許多家長而言是一大吸引力。」
哈羅公學及貝德福德學校是印度少數提供完整劍橋課程（Cambridge curriculum）的學校之一，涵蓋小學至高考（A-level）階段。劍橋課程是一套全球教育體系，目前獲全球約10,000所學校採用。
哈爾西姆蘭·辛格·科查爾（Harsimran Singh Kocchar）的大家族本身就在印度經營連鎖學校，但他仍決定把五歲女兒帕麗妮特（Parineet）送入莫哈利的貝德福德學校。
他表示，原因在於學校「重視品格培養及自信，而不只是學業成績」。
辛格又說，吸引他的另一個因素，是學校不像許多印度同類學校般存在「VIP文化」。
他說：「所有孩子都被一視同仁對待。部長和高級官員的子女不會享有較多特權。」
帕斯科表示，除了愈來愈多富裕的本地家庭外，海外印度人亦是這些學校的重要市場，包括長年在外國生活後回流印度的人士，以及仍居於英國或中東、希望子女保持與印度文化聯繫的家庭。
哈羅公學班加羅爾校區有60%的教職員來自海外。與其他英國公學一樣，該校把自身獨特傳統帶到印度校園。教師被稱為「Beaks」，學生穿着傳統哈羅帽和校服，並參加「The Long Ducker」跨國賽跑，該活動在哈羅全球各校同步舉行。
校內亦設有英式教育標誌性的「學院制度」。
這些充滿英國傳統色彩的校園文化，同時融入印度本地習俗，例如每天早上齊唱印度國歌，以及慶祝印度教重要節日象神節（Ganesh Chaturthi）。
印度不斷增強的經濟實力，以及迅速增加的新晉百萬富翁人口，為英國公學擴張提供了有利條件，但這波增長部分亦是受到中國市場放緩所推動。
過去十年間，英國公學海外擴張很大程度上依賴中國和香港市場。目前由50所英國學校營運的151個海外分校校區中，有一半位於中國和香港。
不過，根據英國智庫「私立教育政策論壇」（Private Education Policy Forum，PEPF）於2025年發表的研究，隨着監管政策改變，以及各國政府加強審查甚至出現抗拒態度，相關增長已經放緩。
PEPF指出，中國於2024年實施的新法例要求學校將愛國主義教育融入所有學科，進一步增加海外學校在中國發展的挑戰，甚至導致部分原定興建的校園計劃被取消。這促使有關學校開始考慮印度和越南等其他市場。
此外，英國在2024年秋季財政預算案中宣布對私立學校學費徵收20%增值稅（VAT）。莫哈利貝德福德學校（Bedford School Mohali）創校校長娜歐蜜·阿特金斯（Naomi Atkins）表示，這項措施迫使許多私立學校尋求海外發展機會。
她向BBC表示：「它們正處於非常艱難的處境。即使是過去從未考慮國際擴張的學校，如今也突然開始積極進入印度市場。」
不過，阿特金斯承認，印度並非一個容易開拓的市場。
這些學校大多透過與當地投資者或營運商合作設立分校。
阿特金斯表示，過去在其他國家，英國學校一般可從合作夥伴收取相當於收入10%的費用，但在印度，利潤率在某些情況下可能低至僅1%。
她又表示，部分學校亦高估了印度市場的規模。
儘管印度有接近2.5億名在學學生，但英語教育早已深深植根當地，來自本土學校的競爭遠較中國、韓國或越南等非英語國家激烈得多。
此外，印度人均收入仍然較低，而英國學校的高昂學費亦限制了增長空間。部分學校的全寄宿學費可高達15,000英鎊甚至更高。
阿特金斯說：「我曾在印尼、馬來西亞和中國工作，但印度人對價格敏感得多，他們喜歡尋找划算的選擇。」
正因如此，莫哈利貝德福德學校的學費約為其他英國學校的一半。
根據PEPF數據，2011/12學年至2022/23學年間，英國學校海外分校共錄得1.524億英鎊利潤，而且相關收益多年來顯著增長。
不過，在印度，這些學校的發展看來更可能是緩慢而穩定，而非爆發式增長。
印度的殖民歷史背景，以及新興富裕階層的崛起，確實為這些歷史悠久的英國學校帶來可觀的商機，但至少在短期內，這個市場規模仍不足以彌補中國市場萎縮造成的損失。
我們使用了人工智慧協助翻譯這篇文章，它的原文是英文。在發佈之前，BBC記者檢查了翻譯的內容。

items.title: 德语媒体：消沉的中国年轻一代
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：消沉的中国年轻一代/a-79767039?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 《新苏黎世报》长篇评论称，在就业困境和社会重压之下，很多中国年轻人正在对未来失去信心。而弥漫在年轻人当中的颓废氛围，也给习近平的“强国梦”带来了挑战。《明镜》周刊评论写道，面对可能形成的中美俄“三巨头”格局，欧盟应利用中美两国对欧洲市场的依赖，以强硬姿态阻止任何有损欧洲利益的协定。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《新苏黎世报》评论写道，北京的咖啡馆里，一段时间以来总是人满为患。不过，他们当中的很多人并不是在消磨休闲时光，而是一些不愿让家人知道自己已经失业的年轻人：他们早上离家，在咖啡馆逗留一天，晚上再回家。以此营造早九晚五照常上班的假象。这篇题为《颓废的中国年轻一代》的评论写道：
“中国年轻一代的情绪很久没有像现在这样糟糕了，原因之一是就业市场的不景气状况。招人的企业很少，裁员的企业很多。很多企业非但不涨薪，反而在削减工资，并要求员工增加工时。一段时间以来，甚至有企业要求新入职员工签署意向书，同意每隔两周就有一天周末加班。雇主这样的做法在网上引发众怒之后，有关当局很快就关闭了微信上的相关讨论。
企业不愿招聘员工的主要原因是中国经济的持续低迷以及严重的内需疲软。作为中国经济曾经的支柱，房地产行业一直无法走出危机，而同美国和欧盟的贸易战更令中国经济雪上加霜。
政府大力推动的人工智能也为年轻人的就业前景蒙上了阴影。阿里巴巴和字节跳动等高科技企业已经缩减了员工规模，尽管他们并没有承认裁员同人工智能有关。然而，了解企业内幕的专家则证实，人工智能是推动企业精简的关键因素。其他一些行业中，人工智能的使用也导致了裁员。”
《新苏黎世报》的评论指出，在16岁至24岁的年轻人当中，失业率已经达到接近20%的程度。失业对中国年轻一代的冲击之大可想而知，因为他们成长在中国快速发展的年代。每一代人都能实现生活水平的大幅提升，几乎被当作了理所当然的事情：
“然而，过去的认知现在已经不再适用。对于年轻一代来说，找一份体面的工作、买一套住房、组建一个家庭，这些原本以为笃定能够实现的梦想，现在已经破灭了。年轻人当中，愤怒、不解和担忧情绪正在快速蔓延。邓小平开启中国改革开放路线五十年之后，史无前例的经济腾飞正在面临一场时代性的转折。
而不确定的经济前景，并不是让年轻人感到沮丧的唯一原因。罹患严重心理疾病和焦虑情绪的人越来越多。一项对中国名牌大学1300名学生进行的问卷调查显示，家庭的过高期望、成绩压力以及就业市场的残酷竞争，已经令很多年轻学子感到不堪重负。很多受访者表示，他们已经陷入了‘焦虑和精神瘫痪状态’。
政府过去几十年来快速推进的现代化进程，其高昂的代价现在正在逐渐显露。许多人感到压力过大。其结果是，越来越多具有聪明才智的年轻人正在退出经济生活。习近平原本希望年轻一代能带领中国实现强国梦，但现如今， 他们却在挫败和疲惫中选择当了逃兵。”
必须阻止”三巨头“损害欧洲利益
对于俄罗斯总统普京有关今年十一月在中国深圳举行中美俄三方会谈商讨乌克兰问题的建议，《明镜》周刊发表评论写道，普京试图同特朗普和习近平结成一个危险的联盟，而欧盟有能力阻止这一切的发生：
“欧洲人在制定战略规划时，必须考虑到未来普京利用乌克兰资源来对付欧洲的可能性。为了避免这种情形的出现，欧洲必须让拟议中的‘三巨头’清楚一点，欧洲不仅能够忍受痛苦，也有能力让对方感受到痛苦。为此目的，欧洲可以动用贸易武器，毕竟中国和美国都离不开欧洲市场。
今年十月初，欧洲人的贸易杠杆就在北京取得了成功，中国在保护欧洲汽车工业问题上最终做出了让步。而在今年一月，欧洲人亮出了王牌：欧盟反胁迫工具，最终迫使特朗普放弃了吞并格陵兰岛的狂热计划。德国总理默茨和法国总统马克龙前不久还提出了进一步强化贸易工具的建议。这说明了一个道理：在一个瞬息万变的世界里，谁不能保护自身利益，谁就将成为失败者。
在特朗普和普京进一步达成损害乌克兰利益的协议之前，尤其是可能的深圳中美俄三方会谈之前，欧洲的政治领袖们必须亮明立场：任何有损欧洲经济利益的协议，都将受到欧盟最强有力的回击。尽管从法律层面而言，贸易政策工具只能用来应对贸易冲突，而不能用来对付无法认同的地缘政治走势。但当前局势使我们有足够理由采取变通态度。例如，欧盟可以考虑制裁更多向俄罗斯侵略者提供物资的中国企业。这类制裁当然也会让欧洲人蒙受损失，但如果欧洲人继续袖手旁观，最终必将蒙受更大的痛苦。”

items.title: 被欧盟指控销售不安全商品 TEMU承诺整改
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/被欧盟指控销售不安全商品-temu承诺整改/a-79766979?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 今年5月，欧盟委员会对中国跨境电商平台TEMU处以2亿欧元罚款，指控其未能充分保护消费者免受违规产品的威胁。现在，TEMU向欧盟委员会提交方案承诺整改，后者已经认可了这些措施。TEMU现在有4个月时间来予以落实。
items.content:
被欧盟指控销售不安全商品 TEMU承诺整改
2026年10月26日
（德国之声中文网）根据欧盟委员会10月26日发布的消息，来自中国的TEMU已经同意今后基于最新的可靠数据来对其电商平台系统进行量身定做的风险评估。同时，TEMU的推荐算法也要进行审核。公司必须提供可靠指标，以证明这一系列保护措施是否有效减少了违法商品的传播；TEMU还必须披露：其针对平台上入驻商户的自动审核及人工审核是否存在局限性、这些局限性又体现在哪些方面。这家来自中国的电商平台还必须自行调查入驻商户如何蓄意利用平台功能传播违法商品信息。
今年5月，Temu遭到了欧盟委员会的2亿欧元罚款，被指控未能充分保护消费者免受违法产品的侵害，并低估了其平台上存在的风险。欧盟委员会表示，这严重违反了欧盟《数字服务法》(DSA)。
欧盟方面称，在2025年进行的测试购买中，许多不合格商品都在平台上顺利交易。比如，极高比例的小型电子设备及充电器未能通过基本的安全测试，而接受测试的婴儿玩具中，“相当大比例”的商品要么超过了化学安全限值，要么由于可拆卸部件而存在窒息风险。负责技术主权与安全的欧盟委员会副主席维尔库宁(Henna Virkkunen)指出，TEMU目前在欧洲拥有高达1.3亿用户，这意味着大量违法产品正流入众多欧盟公民手中。
根据欧盟委员会的通报，TEMU的整改方案已经得到了初步接受，现在有4个月时间来具体落实这些措施。如果届时欧盟委员会认定TEMU没有采取足够措施来遵守欧盟法规，将会对这家中国企业再追加额外的每日罚款。
欧盟近年来一直试图采取措施来遏制中国廉价小商品通过TEMU、Shein、速卖通(AliExpress)等电商平台流入欧洲市场。就在7月1日，欧盟开始对所有来自中国的小包裹加征3欧元的统一关税，以前此类包裹享有免税待遇。

本月初，在博索纳罗赢得首轮投票后，巴西股市曾一度飙升至历史高点。到了周一，股市又跌回到大约大选前的水平。
美国2008年次贷危机和2020年新冠疫情期间，巴西也曾启动过熔断机制。

items.description: 奥迪首席执行官德尔纳上周六在美国佐治亚州登上特朗普的竞选集会舞台，宣布奥迪将在当地投资约40亿美元建设首座美国工厂。德国金属行业工会和大众集团职工委员会指责他违反公司选举前保持政治中立的规定。有德国汽车专家称德尔纳是"迷你版马斯克"。
items.content:
奥迪CEO现身竞选集会挺特朗普 德国工会怒批违反中立规定
2026年10月26日
（德国之声中文网）周一（10月26日），奥迪首席执行官德尔纳（Gernot Doellner）因在美国总统特朗普的竞选集会上露面而遭到德国工会猛烈批评。
上周六（10月24日），德尔纳出席了特朗普在关键摇摆州佐治亚州梅肯（Macon）附近举行的共和党竞选活动。特朗普在集会上宣布，奥迪将在当地建设首座美国工厂，年产20万辆SUV。德尔纳随后登台，感谢特朗普的支持。据报道，奥迪称该项目将创造约4500个就业岗位。
工会：公然违反中立规定
德国金属行业工会（IG Metall）主席、大众监事会副主席本纳（Christiane Benner）说，德尔纳的露面"极其令人难堪，在政治上不可接受，也有损公司的形象"，"公然违反"了奥迪在选举前保持政治中立的承诺。奥迪的行为准则规定，选举前三个月内不得与参选政党或候选人公开互动，也不得赞助此类活动。美国中期选举将于11月3日举行。
大众集团职工委员会主席卡瓦洛（Daniela Cavallo）也严厉批评德尔纳。她说，特朗普在台上发表了"几分钟充满种族主义、性别歧视、仇外心理"的言论，随后"我们集团的一名高管就登台积极助选"。她还说，德尔纳几个月前刚签署过这些准则，并批评大众首席执行官布鲁姆（Oliver Blume）领导下的董事会沦为特朗普"宣传秀的木偶"。
德国汽车专家杜登霍费尔（Ferdinand Dudenhoeffer）称德尔纳是"迷你版马斯克"。特朗普此前曾表态支持德国极右翼政党德国选择党，这使他成为德国政商主流眼中颇具争议的盟友。
建厂计划：商业上合理，但待监事会拍板
工会强调，这项投资尚未获大众集团相关机构全部批准，最终须由大众监事会决定。卡瓦洛认为，美国市场规模大、利润高，在美建厂从商业角度看有其道理，但员工代表只有在弄清新厂对德国等地工厂的影响后，才会考虑批准。
据路透社报道，奥迪去年因美国进口关税损失约12亿欧元。与此同时，大众正在推进裁员10万人的计划，雇员约1.5万人的奥迪内卡苏尔姆工厂面临关闭风险。梅茨勒银行（Metzler）分析师说，在全球削减产能的同时在美国创造就业，"观感不佳"，但在美生产的决定是正确的。

items.title: “中国人民的老朋友”日本前首相福田康夫去世
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中国人民的老朋友-日本前首相福田康夫去世/a-79765385?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 日本前首相福田康夫当地时间10月22日去世，享年90岁。中国政府在第一时间向他的家属致以诚挚慰问，并称“福田康夫先生是中国人民的老朋友”。
items.content:
“中国人民的老朋友”日本前首相福田康夫去世
2026年10月26日
（德国之声中文网）福田康夫曾于2007年至2008年担任日本第91任首相，在任365天。他出生于1936年，其父福田赳夫也曾担任日本首相，并曾致力于推动东京与北京之间关系的发展。
福田康夫毕业于东京早稻田大学政经学系。在投身政坛前，曾在一家日本石油公司工作了17年。1976年，在其父出任日本首相前夕，福田康夫开始担任父亲的私人秘书。
1990年，福田康夫首次当选国会议员。之后担任多个与外交相关的职务，并被视为外交专家。与他父亲一样，福田康夫非常重视与亚洲国家建立友好关系。2000年，他在时任首相森喜朗内阁中担任内阁官房长官，即政府首席发言人。由于经常需要为频频失言的森喜朗对外做出说明，福田康夫当时自嘲自己是“辩解长官”。
2007年，时任首相安倍晋三突然宣布辞职。当时已71岁的福田康夫获得自民党内多数派支持，参选并当选自民党总裁，随后出任日本第91任首相。执政期间，福田康夫与时任中国国家主席胡锦涛建立了稳定的关系。由于自民党仅在众议院拥有多数席位，而在参议院不占优势，福田康夫面临诸多挑战，最终仅在任一年便卸任。
2012年退休后，福田康夫致力于改善日中关系。当时，两国关系正因钓鱼岛及其附属岛屿（日称尖阁诸岛）的领土争端而陷入冰期。 2014年，福田康夫访问中国并与中国国家主席习近平举行会谈，为时任日本首相的安倍晋三访华并与习近平会晤铺平了道路。
2022年，在纪念日中邦交正常化50周年之际，福田康夫在接受美联社采访时表示：“缺少对话会增加误解的风险……在正常情况下本不会发生的事情，也可能会发生。”
福田康夫平日里常板着脸，但也以其独特的冷幽默而著称。2008年9月宣布辞去首相职务时，有记者指出，他说话的口气听起来仿佛是在谈论别人。福田康夫随即回应道：“我能够客观地审视自己。我可不像你们。”
“我可不像你们”这句话后来入选了2008年某出版机构举办的年度流行语榜单，但福田康夫拒绝领奖。
中国称福田康夫先生是中国人民的老朋友
中国政府在第一时间对福田康夫去世的消息做出回应。中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆26日在例行记者会上答问时表示，中方对福田康夫前首相逝世表示沉痛哀悼，向他的家属致以诚挚慰问，并称“福田康夫先生是中国人民的老朋友”，为推动中日关系改善发展作出积极贡献。“
郭嘉昆指出，福田康夫担任首相期间签署了中日之间第四份政治文件，卸任后参观了侵华日军南京大屠杀遇难同胞纪念馆。他还曾长期担任博鳌亚洲论坛理事长，为促进亚洲地区交流合作发挥了重要作用。郭嘉昆还引用福田康夫称，中日四个政治文件规定了两国关系遵循的原则，必须时刻牢记，不能走回头路，并敦促”日本当政者应当深思自省“。

6 US citizens sue Trump, saying media ban deprives them of news as audience stakeholders
The lawsuit argues that the White House ban violates the public’s right to independent reporting about its president and government
In the increasingly bitter legal stand-off between US President Donald Trump and media outlets whose reporting he dislikes, a new and crucial third party has emerged: citizens who watch and read the news and need it to do their jobs.
A lawsuit filed on Monday on behalf of six such citizens – effectively representing the audiences for the news media – argues that it is not only the rights of news organisations that are violated when Trump bans them from White House premises.
Even more fundamentally, the lawsuit argues, such bans violate the public’s right to independent reporting about its president and government.

The 18-year-old student was fatally stabbed in Southampton in December by Vickrum Digwa, who falsely claimed he had been racially abused and had acted in self-defence. Digwa was jailed for life on 1 June, with a minimum term of 21 years.
Following the teenager's murder, police bodycam footage of him being handcuffed as he lay dying led to intense scrutiny of the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary and sparked wider debates around knife laws, race, policing and public trust.
The review, which was welcomed by Nowak's family, will be led by former Justice Secretary Alex Chalk KC.
"We must get to truth of what happened before, during and after that awful night and we must do everything in our power to ensure that no family suffers the same fate," Mahmood told the House of Commons on Monday.
Mahmood said the review will investigate what was known about Nowak's killer and if there were missed opportunities to intervene as well as the treatment of his family in the justice system and whether they received enough support.
In a statement published on Monday, the Home Office said the review will be carried out in two parts.
Phase one will cover the police, health services, local authorities educational institutions and faith organisations, including if any concerns were raised relating to weapon possession and violent behavior, the statement said.
It will also look to determine if there were missed opportunities to prevent Nowak's murder.
Phase two will follow after the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has concluded its investigation into the actions of police officers who attended the scene.
It will consider the actions of the IOPC and "if necessary" the police, the Home Office added.
The IOPC launched its own investigation into the response on the night of Nowak's death after bodycam footage showed the 18-year-old was handcuffed and left dying on the floor despite informing officers of his injuries.
The investigation was launched despite a sentencing judge ruling Nowak would not have survived his injuries, however quickly he received treatment.
The Nowak family described the announcement as a "significant moment in our fight for justice."
"We hope this review, alongside the ongoing investigations and inquest, will finally uncover the full truth and deliver the accountability and meaningful change we have fought so hard for," they added in a statement.
"Our experience of the criminal justice system has been deeply disappointing, and we are determined that no other family should have to endure what we have."
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch welcomed the decision to launch the review.
"There must be proper accountability for those who failed Henry and his family," she said.
The review is due to report in five months.
Nowak, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was a first-year accountancy and finance student at the University of Southampton when he was murdered.
On the night of Nowak's muder, it was Digwa's brother who called 999, claiming Vickrum had been attacked "racially".
Bodycam footage released by Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary, with the permission of Nowak's family, showed officers speaking to Digwa and others while Nowak lay on the ground.
Nowak could be heard repeatedly saying that he had been stabbed and could not breathe.
Violent disorder broke out in Southampton in the days following the release of the footage.
After Digwa's sentencing, Nowak's father Mark called for a "full, fearless and transparent" investigation into the police response.
But he also urged people not to use his son's death to "create further division, hatred or tension".

items.title: Israel and the US are both going to the polls - the consequences will be global
items.description: The next fortnight sees two elections on different continents. The outcomes will shape geopolitics and the global economy, writes James Landale
items.content:
In the next week, two sets of elections will be held on two continents, the outcomes of which could have profound consequences for the world.
By a fluke of electoral timetabling, millions of voters around 6,000 miles apart will unite in exercising their democratic rights within days of each other.
Voters in Israel go to the polls on Tuesday to elect a new parliament; a week later, voters in the United States will elect a new Congress.
A former speaker of that Congress, Tip O'Neill, may have once said that "all politics is local". But the consequences of these elections will undoubtedly be global.
For these elections are not just proximate, they are intertwined.
The future governance of Israel will have a lasting impact on the Middle East and wars raging across the region.
And any change in the electoral map of America could shape not just those wars but also the future of the global economy.
Between the two there is a physical connection: the lobby group Republicans Overseas Israel estimates about half a million Israelis with American passports can vote in both polls.
Marc Zell, the group's chairman, said these electors could influence tight races in the US, such as the Michigan senatorial contest, in which he estimated 10,000 absentee ballots would be cast from Israel. "They can really make a difference," he told the BBC.
But the policy connection is perhaps deeper - and most acute regarding the US-Israeli war on Iran. The massive aerial attack, which began in February, destroyed many military targets and killed much of Iran's leadership. But it failed to overthrow the regime which hit back hard across the Gulf and seized control of the Strait of Hormuz and the energy that flowed through it.
The Iran question
The sheer fact of the elections has already shaped decision-making.
Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has used the campaign to talk up the possibility of launching a fresh attack on Iran.
He has made new claims – without providing evidence – about Iran's nuclear threat, insisting again the Islamic regime must be overthrown.
His aim: to shore up his reputation as a security leader, which took such a battering after the deadly 7 October Hamas-led attacks on Israel.
US President Donald Trump has added to the speculation of renewed attacks on Iran by endorsing Netanyahu's re-election campaign, saying both men should "soon finish the job" in Iran.
Yet for all the sabre-rattling, there have also been contradictory reports that Trump intervened to restrain Netanyahu from attacking Iran before polling day, fearing a fresh spike in energy prices would remind US voters of his unpopular war.
So might an attack on Iran, then, be delayed until after the elections? Israel's media is full of speculation Netanyahu could try to engineer his survival by attacking Iran as caretaker prime minister after the election.
He would argue, so the theory goes, for a government of national unity – involving him – rather than a coalition between opposition parties. Netanyahu has long been seen as a great survivor of Israeli politics. If he were to lose power, he would face an official inquiry into his actions before the October 7 attacks and renewed legal proceedings involving allegations of corruption.
So real is this speculation that Netanyahu's rival, the former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has already ruled out joining any unity government. Like all mainstream Israeli politicians, Eisenkot sees Iran as an existential threat to Israel and supports military action against the Islamic regime. But he has explicitly warned against escalating the war for political purposes.
'Legacy mode'
Certainly, Trump may be more willing to attack Iran after the midterms if he is unconstrained electorally and hoping to extract himself from the war with one more push. Some analysts believe Iran is so economically weak from the war and economic sanctions that a fresh round of military strikes might encourage Iranians to overthrow the regime. Others see this as yet more wishful thinking. It is a strategy that has repeatedly failed, but still has currency in Washington.
"After the midterms, he will be in legacy mode," one well-placed Western diplomat told me. "He will want to show agency on anything that is not the quagmire at home."
In Israel there is a broad consensus across most parties about the threat from and the need to constrain Iran. But if voters elect a new government, they might have a prime minister with less political and personal investment in fresh attacks.
In those circumstances, Trump has suggested his thinking may change, too. "If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi [a nickname for Netanyahu], America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so," he wrote on social media.
Little wonder policymakers in Tehran have been following US opinion polls as closely as any analyst inside the Washington beltway. The risk, of course, is that any post-electoral strikes would plunge the Middle East into fresh chaos if Iran were to retaliate hard.
Publicly and privately, Iranian officials have threatened to hit airports, pipelines, undersea cables, energy facilities, desalination plants as well as US bases and warships.
Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, wrote in the Financial Times that new attacks would put "civilian lives and the wellbeing of all regional states and the global economy at great risk".
It's the economy
The two elections again intertwine around the global economy. Affordability and cost of living have dominated campaigning for the midterms, issues made worse by Trump's war that raised prices as Iran choked the flow of energy through the Strait of Hormuz.
The economy is also an election issue in Israel, where voters face high costs and low wages. But here, too, the war plays its part with soaring defence spending putting even more pressure on the public finances.
Trump has sought to appease voters ahead of the midterms. He has lifted sanctions on Russia, hoping in vain that by importing diesel from Moscow, prices might fall significantly. He has been taking a tough line with Ukraine, calling on its leadership to make concessions in the hope – also so far in vain – of claiming a foreign policy victory.
But Republican ire at his controversial strategy is growing. Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina, a frequent critic of Trump, told CBS News: "If the President wants to actually bring down energy prices, he can do it by solving the Iran problem, not by doing a solid [favour] for Vladimir Putin."
One consequence of the Iran war – along with Israel's military operations in Gaza and the occupied West Bank – is that traditional bipartisan support in the US has fractured. Abdul El-Sayed, the left-wing Democratic candidate for the Senate in Michigan, campaigns on cutting military aid to Israel. "An ally that takes your money, to push you into wars you shouldn't be fighting, is not an ally," he told ABC News.
The US and Israel initially attacked Iran to destroy its ballistic missiles, degrade its nuclear capability, weaken its support for proxy militias and even oust the entire regime. Since then its war aims have changed to reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Brad Lander, a Democratic congressional candidate in New York who also sits on the left of his party, chose even to travel to the West Bank only days before polling. He helped Palestinians harvest olives and was briefly detained by Israeli forces, all grist to his social media electoral mill. In the history of US politics, this is not normal. Even Netanyahu is warning that Israel may in future have to survive without a US security blanket.
Of course, if Israel's prime minister were to lose, his departure would end a scratchy bromance that has seen Trump blow hot and cold. Last week the president called his Israeli counterpart a "great warrior prime minister". During the summer, he said Netanyahu was "effing crazy". A new Israeli leader would have to forge a new relationship with an outgoing US president, a very different dynamic.
If the Democrats were to win greater control in Congress, that might place some check on blanket US support for Israel. Congress has traditional powers that it can use to restrain military spending. It could also cut military aid to Israel. But as president, Trump would retain significant executive power – and a veto – to continue prosecuting the conflict as he saw fit.
The decision by Israel and the US to go to war with Iran earlier this year transformed the global economy and international geopolitics. The choices voters in both nations make in coming days may shape where the world goes next.

items.title: Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed
items.description: Justyna Hulboj and her daughter Lena died when they were hit by a car in Leeds in January 2023.
items.content:
Drivers who killed mum and girl while racing jailed
- Published
Two men who killed a mother and her four-year-old daughter as they raced their high-performance cars along a Leeds city centre road have been jailed.
Justyna Hulboj, 27, and her daughter Lena Czepczor were killed when they were hit by an Audi TT RS as they walked to the girl's nursery on the A61 Scott Hall Road on 16 January 2023.
At Leeds Crown Court on Monday, Hardeep Bhachu, 29, was jailed for 12 years and Jasskamal Riyat, 37, for 16 years.
Sentencing the men, Judge Singh said the road was "not a race track" and told them the deaths had consequences that were "immeasurable", with an "immense" impact on those left behind.
Bhachu, of Grant Row in Adel, had earlier admitted two counts of causing death by dangerous driving, while Riyat, of Buckstone Avenue in Moortown, was convicted by a jury after denying he had been racing him.
The court heard the pair, who did not previously know each other, accelerated away from traffic lights on Scott Hall Road shortly before the crash.
Prosecutors said Riyat's BMW reached speeds of up to 89mph in the 40mph zone before Bhachu lost control of his Audi, mounted the pavement and struck Hulboj and her daughter.
Judge Singh said the victims had "done nothing wrong" and were "simply walking to school".
Addressing the defendants, he said: "A road is not a race track. A powerful car is not an invitation to test its limits on a public road.
"The consequences of competitive driving at extreme speed can be, and in this case were, irreversible."
He added: "Justyna and Lena should have gone to school that morning. They should have returned home. They should have continued with their lives.
"Instead, their lives ended on a pavement because two drivers chose to drive in a manner which placed speed and competition above the safety of everyone around them."
Susannah Proctor, for Bhachu, told the court that her client was a "normal person who's made a massive mistake".
She said he "must live with himself in the knowledge of the devastation he has caused".
And she said: "He did not intend to cause this devastation but cause it he has."
Hulboj's fiancé Dominik Czepczor watched the sentencing hearing in court.
A statement from him was read, which said: "My whole world collapsed in one second.
"Every day I feel a huge void after their departure.
"We had so many hopes and dreams and in one moment it all ended.
"My dream was to have a wonderful family, and I must say that it came true for a short while, but that was taken away from me on January 16.
"Unfortunately, all that remains are wonderful memories and a constant fight for the next day, which is not easy."
Det Insp Paul Conroy, of West Yorkshire Police's Major Collision Enquiry Team, said: "A woman and her young daughter have died because of the actions of these men, and I know no sentence will ever feel enough to compensate for the lives that have been lost.
"This sentencing hearing though does mark the end of a long criminal justice process for Justyna and Lena's family.
"It is over two years since Bhachu admitted his part in this tragic incident and I know that the wait for justice has taken its toll.
"My thoughts are firmly with them today."

items.title: Storm Boelo leaves 22,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning
items.description: The Met Office has issued a fresh wind warning from 18:00 on Monday across the west coast of England, Wales and Scotland and eastern parts of Northern Ireland.
items.content:
Storm Boelo leaves 22,000 without power as Met Office issues new wind warning
- Published
A clean-up operation is under way in parts of the UK after Storm Boelo caused flooding and property damage, leaving thousands without power.
The Energy Networks Association (ENA) said around 22,600 properties are still without power as of Monday afternoon.
Two men were killed by falling trees during the storm on Sunday - a man in his 20s whose car was hit in north London and a 60-year-old man in Dumfries and Galloway identified as Richard Baines, the long-serving curator of Logan Botanic Garden.
The Met Office has issued a yellow warning for strong winds from 18:00 on Monday to 03:00 on Tuesday across the west coast of England, Wales and Scotland and eastern parts of Northern Ireland.
The Met Office has warned that further power cuts in areas covered by the warning are likely and people should make sure they have essentials prepared, including torches and batteries.
Coastal communities could also be affected by spray or large waves, while travel delays are expected.
Boelo is the second storm to have hit parts of the UK in recent days, following Storm Austen.
Leo Slade, CEO of the ENA said it had been "a tough weekend" and that efforts to reconnect some properties were being hampered by the weather, with sustained winds of 50-85mph across parts of Scotland and northern England.
"Until that weather system passes, we can't safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up, so today is going to be a hive of activity in getting engineers out into the field," Slade told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
He stressed that the UK's power network was very resilient and money was spent to prepare for these sorts of scenarios, but said a debate was needed over how much more investment was required to mitigate for further storms brought by climate change.
- Storm Boelo clears but more wind and rain bears down on UK 
  - Published9 hours ago
Marcus Reed, the operations director at a home fragrance manufacturer, said his factory and shop in Lyndal, Cumbria would be without power until Tuesday evening.
He told the Today programme that he has had to turn away employees and customers.
"To lose two days manufacturing and distribution is going to be really disruptive," he said, adding that it was bad timing as it was "the busiest time of the year" for his business in the lead-up to Christmas.
"This is probably the worst situation I've experienced in my time here; we've had ad hoc issues over weekends where we've lost power, but it's been contained within a 12-hour period. It's the first time anything like this has happened, it's very serious."
Wendy McKinney, whose bathroom shop in the seaside town of Largs in North Ayrshire was flooded on Sunday, told the Today programme the storm had been "devastating to local businesses".
She said the local council only handed out sandbags after flooding had already started:"[They] were just left in the middle of the street yesterday afternoon on pallets just for everybody just to try and help themselves, but it was too little too late."
North Ayrshire Council told the BBC that it had distributed almost 300 sandbags in Largs and Saltcoats and would continue to "respond where it has been safe and appropriate to do so".
A spokesperson said council teams "followed established resilience procedures" but would review flooding reports and "consider any lessons that can be learned".
Disruption to travel has continued on Monday, and some schools in Scotland have been shut either due to lack of power, heating, water or damage.
Another yellow warning of wind, external has been issued by the Met Office, covering much of Scotland, as well as parts of northern England and Northern Ireland from 03:00 to 23:59 on Tuesday.
Monday morning has seen rain in many parts of south-west England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and this is moving north-eastwards reaching central, eastern and northern England, as well as most of Scotland, by around lunchtime.
Winds will also strengthen throughout Monday, and it will turn even windier overnight as the area of low pressure passes close to Northern Ireland and north-west Scotland with gusts peaking on Tuesday.

items.title: How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around
items.description: Millions joined a 'Lula's Army' channel that helped to transform online enthusiasm into real-world mobilisation.
items.content:
How 'Lula's Army' WhatsApp channel helped turn Brazil election around
- Published
A WhatsApp channel created to support Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election campaign is being credited by allies with helping deliver one of the most unlikely comebacks in recent Brazilian politics.
Brazil's left-wing president had been trailing right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, but managed to turn the race around in just three weeks.
The rise of 'Lula's Army'
At a moment when many doubted Lula could reverse the result, a WhatsApp channel called Lula's Army emerged, and rapidly grew to 10.8 million followers.
Led by Congressman André Janones, the operation encouraged supporters to share videos, promote hashtags and recruit new voters.
Its dramatic growth between the two rounds was particularly notable because it appeared to reverse a long-standing imbalance in Brazilian politics.
For years, conservatives aligned with former President Jair Bolsonaro had been widely seen as dominating online political mobilisation, especially on platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram.
The emergence of Lula's Army convinced many supporters that Brazil's left had finally found a way to compete in a digital arena. The shift was particularly significant because social media has played a central role in Brazilian politics since Jair Bolsonaro's 2018 election victory, when WhatsApp networks became a defining feature of political campaigning.
Lula's Army messages often included ready-made templates for followers to share with friends and family. Each one assigned supporters a specific task aimed at boosting Lula's visibility on social media.
Janones frequently instructed his "troops" to "blow up" the latest campaign video or help a new hashtag "take off".
"Guys, urgent!", "Don't go to sleep yet", "No food before the mission!", and "I have one more task before you're dismissed", were some of the instructions.
On the eve of the election, the congressman also hosted a 24-hour live event - dubbed the "turnaround livestream" - even as polls continued to suggest a victory for Bolsonaro.
The tactic worked, despite worries by some members of the Workers' Party that Janones's often-confrontational style on social media could undermine the more moderate image they hoped to project for Lula.
In his victory speech, Lula referred to Janones as "our General" and thanked him for "raising the morale of our troops every day".
Social media's role in the comeback
Measuring the electoral impact of online mobilisation, however, is notoriously difficult.
While Lula's allies credit Lula's Army with helping fuel the comeback, political scientists caution that it is impossible to determine how many votes, if any, were directly influenced by the WhatsApp operation.
Political scientist Denilde Holzhacker argues that a shift in Lula's campaign strategy was key to his comeback.
Rather than relying solely on online engagement, she says the Workers' Party candidate succeeded in connecting digital campaigning with grassroots mobilisation on the ground.
According to Holzhacker, the campaign intensified local efforts and adapted its messaging - linking a Bolsonaro victory with concerns about potential changes to social programmes and the loss of rights.
"It was to Lula's credit that he recognised his own weakness and completely changed his style," she says. "And Janones managed to do something that had seemed unthinkable for Brazil's left - dominate social media."
By contrast, Holzhacker argues that Flávio Bolsonaro entered the run-off overly confident of victory and failed to communicate his message to his supporters as effectively.
Sociologist and political scientist Mayra Goulart, a professor at the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, also cautions against attributing Lula's comeback solely to social media.
"It was a combination of social media and street-level mobilisation," she says. "The physical world enabled a form of mobilisation capable of reducing abstention and persuading undecided voters."
In her view, Lula's supporters succeeded in turning online enthusiasm into real-world political engagement.
"Those committed to Lula's victory worked to bring people together and persuade them to vote," Goulart says.
She argues that the effort not only helped increase turnout but could also prove valuable for Lula's next administration.
"I believe this collective effort was an important learning experience and will prove valuable for a government that still faces many battles ahead. It not only helped reduce abstention, but also converted a significant number of undecided voters."
Lula himself suggested that the mobilisation behind his comeback could shape the way he governs in the years ahead.
In his victory speech, he said the election had taught him many lessons and pledged to change the way Brazil is governed.
"We are going to give people a greater say in decision-making, and digital communication will play a much bigger role in my government."

items.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
items.content:
Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.
Link Copied!
Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
Link Copied!
Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.
Link Copied!
Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment
From CNN's Kristen Holmes
From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

Photos: Trump arrives in New York City a day before his expected arraignment
From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.
Former President Donald Trump waves to supporters upon arriving at Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3. Trump is in New York for an expected arraignment on Tuesday.
(Yuki Iwamura/AP)
Trump's plane lands at LaGuardia Airport in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Timothy Fadek for CNN)
Dan Ray waves an American flag as a plane carrying former President Donald Trump takes off from the Palm Beach International Airport in Florida on Monday, April 3. Trump was heading to New York for an expected arraignment on Tuesday.
(Ricardo Arduengo/Reuters)
A television news reporter from Spain is seen outside Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Stephen Voss for CNN)
Trump supporters cheer as his motorcade passes by in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Monday, April 3.
(Wilfredo Lee/AP)

Former president poised to huddle with advisers at Trump Tower
From Jeff Zeleny
A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.
Link Copied!
Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say.
